subject: Cost sensitivity and structured rebate proposal for Glomerate
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@glomerate.ai>, Devon Li <devon@glomerate.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Glomerate - post-call recap and a couple of asks

Hi Asha / Devon,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to understand the 2 product paths you’re evaluating and the bursty-inference profile you mentioned. Quick recap + two asks so we can put a practical pricing sketch together.

Recap (high level):
- Primary use: conversational agent + reranking for search; 95% of requests are <512 tokens but you have periodic 8k-batch runs for model fine-tuning pipelines.
- Target latency: p95 <= 400ms for interactive flows.
- Timeline: pilot starting late June, production ramp over Q3–Q4.

Asks:
1) Can you confirm a target monthly token volume range for months 1–6 (ballpark is fine) — helps us scope batching/instance sizing.
2) What approval path is needed for a startup credit or committed-use discount (procurement, finance, exec)? Any timing constraints for a legal/PO cycle?

I attached the token forecast template (Glomerate-MAAP-token-forecast.xlsx) you can fill; I’ll use it to produce a $/1M token unit-econ view and a few rebate scenarios.

Next steps: once you confirm the ranges I’ll send a short proposal with: 1) baseline hosted pricing (token tiers), 2) startup credit options, and 3) committed-use / multi-year rebate sketches tied to volume bands.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0148
From: Asha Rao <asha@glomerate.ai>

Thanks Logan — useful recap. Quick answers:

- For months 1–3 we expect 50–150M tokens/mo (pilot), months 4–6 200–700M tokens/mo (ramp). We’ll have occasional month spikes up to ~1.5B tokens during internal load tests.
- Approval path: procurement needs a commercial term sheet + SOC2 evidence; finance needs ballpark $/1M tokens and an estimate of run-rate cost for budgeting. Final sign-off comes from our Head of Product (me) and CFO (Devon).

We’re eligible for early-stage vendor programs; curious what startup credit you can offer and how that stacks with committed discounts. Also timeline: procurement typically needs 2–3 weeks once we have SOW/term sheet.

Asha Rao
Head of Product, Glomerate AI
asha@glomerate.ai

On Apr 11, 2027, at 6:24 PM, Asha Rao wrote:
> Thanks Logan — useful recap. Quick answers: ...

Great — attaching a short pricing sketch (Redwood-rebate-outline.pdf) based on the ranges you provided. High-level proposal below for discussion — all numbers are provisional until we get your detailed forecast.

Baseline hosted pricing (provisional):
- Tier A (0–100M tokens/mo): $1,200 per 1M tokens
- Tier B (100–500M tokens/mo): $850 per 1M tokens
- Tier C (500M+ tokens/mo): $580 per 1M tokens

Startup credit option (early-stage program):
- One-time founder credit: 40% off list for first 3 months (applies to hosted token charges only).
- Eligibility: < $2M annual ARR and seed/series A status (we’ll need simple confirmation).

Committed-use rebate sketches (stackable with startup credit subject to limits):
- 12-month commit (committed tokens invoiced monthly): 10% rebate on billed tokens
- 24-month commit: 15% rebate + 5% additional on overage bands above committed volume in months 13–24
- 36-month commit: 20% rebate + milestone credit (one-time) equal to 10% of initial year spend applied as platform credits in year 2.

Example unit-econ reference (ballpark):
- Baseline (no discounts): $/1M tokens = $1,200 (Tier A)
- With startup credit (40%) applied for 3 months: effective $/1M tokens = $720 for those months
- With 24-month commitment + startup credit (illustrative): effective blended $/1M tokens could be in the $600–$750 range depending on ramp profile and overage treatment.

Operational notes / requirements:
- Volume bands are evaluated monthly; overages billed at the respective tier with rebate applied as per agreement.
- SOC2 report and data retention answers available; I’ll attach the SOC2 summary and point you to evidence in our partner portal if procurement needs it.

If this looks directionally aligned I’ll: 1) ask RevOps (karthik) to model a few specific blended scenarios using your forecast, and 2) route a provisional commercial term sheet (DocuSign link) for procurement.

Would you prefer 24- or 36-month sketches for the commercial term sheet?

—
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Glomerate - pricing sketch + ask for stacking startup credit with commit rebate (need approval)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding the thread. Glomerate (seed-stage, Series A candidate) is asking:

- Confirm they qualify for our 40% founder credit for first 3 months (they indicate early-stage).
- Allow stacking: startup credit + committed-use rebate; proposed stacking would cap at total effective discount of ~60% for year 1 in the 36-month scenario.

Why this matters: they’re projecting a fast ramp (500M+ tokens by month 6) and are procurement-driven (2–3 week legal/PO window). If we can provisionally approve stacking and the 36-month milestone credit we accelerate procurement and increase likelihood of a wider contract.

Request: can we provisionally approve the following exception for GLM-2027-047?
- 40% startup credit for first 3 months (standard conditional doc will be signed)
- Stackable with committed-use rebate up to a combined effective discount not exceeding 60% in year 1; commit tiers as proposed in my sketch.

I’ve attached the Glomerate forecast we used. If you want, I can get a brief legality read from Leah (legal) but procurement wants a term sheet this week.

Thanks — looking for quick thumbs.

—
Logan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hi Asha / Devon — looping in on behalf of Redwood. Appreciate the clear volume ranges; we ran the numbers and can offer the following provisional commercial path to get procurement moving: 

What we can provisionally commit to: 
- Startup founder credit: 40% off hosted token charges for the first 3 months (eligibility confirmed by Asha).
- Commit stacking: startup credit may be applied in addition to committed-use rebates. For Glomerate we will cap combined effective year-1 discount at 60% (this is a commercial cap only).
- Commit options: 24- and 36-month proposals both available; we recommend 36-month if you want the highest blended unit-econ and the one-time milestone credit in year 2.

Next steps:
1) Logan will send a provisional term sheet (DocuSign) with 24- and 36-month worksheets by EOD tomorrow.
2) Please complete the attached forecast and return it to us; procurement can start review once the DocuSign is in play.
3) Legal/Procurement: we’ll include SOC2 summary and a link to evidence; full report available on request.

We’ll mark this as time-sensitive and prioritize RevOps modeling to produce the $/1M blended figures you need for finance.

If that works I’ll route the DocuSign and we’ll set a short 30-minute procurement sync next week.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
